summary: Autoscaler opened node requests but requests queued — reduced throughput in dedicated GPU pool
description: Issue summary: Customer reports sustained request queueing and token throughput drop for their Dedicated pool starting 2026-03-10 02:10 UTC. Autoscaler issued scale-out requests but new nodes did not become usable; requests were queued causing elevated P50/P95 generation latency and occasional 429s. Impact: affecting one enterprise customer's production workflows (real-time summarization), increased tail-latency and some dropped streams. Observed symptoms point to GPU attach/driver issues plus a noisy tenant causing degraded PCIe throughput on a subset of nodes. This ticket captures the investigation, temporary mitigations, and follow-up remediation tasks.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer submits sustained concurrent generation load matching their historical peak: ~120 concurrent sessions targeting redwood-open-7b-v2.
2) Autoscaler evaluates NodeGroup A and requests 3 additional nodes (GPU-backed) to meet queue targets.
3) New node provisioning starts but kubelet reports node Ready false; serving runtime shows GPUs not registered.
4) Requests remain in queue; latency increases and 429 throttles appear between 02:15-02:50 UTC.

comments: 2026-03-10 02:30 - Aisha Patel (Support): Received customer alert. Verified queueing and spikes in latency. Escalating to SRE. Notified #support and #incidents.

2026-03-10 02:45 - Connor Lee (SRE): Observed GPU driver mismatch on two newly provisioned nodes. Kicked node-provisioner to reprovision with correct AMI. Also saw one older node with heavy host-level PCIe traffic tied to tenant-3142.
2026-03-10 03:05 - Miguel Santos (Platform Eng): Driver mismatch caused by an AMI rollback during last maintenance. Rolling forward AMI to fixed build; will cordon and drain failing nodes.

2026-03-10 04:00 - Aisha Patel (Support): Customer confirmed partial recovery after node replacement and temporary bump to overflow capacity. They still see intermittent increased latency during peak window.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Provisioning AMI mismatch (GPU driver) prevented new nodes from registering GPUs. Evidence: kubelet error shows driver mismatch; two failed node attaches.

Hypothesis 2: Noisy neighbor on pool caused PCIe saturations lowering effective throughput of co-located nodes. Evidence: host-level monitoring shows sustained high PCIe Tx/Rx and large NVLINK usage from tenant container PID 8421.
Cloud provider quotas checked: GPU quota available in region. Not a soft quota exhaustion event.
Autoscaler logs: scale-out requests completed but nodes not Ready; autoscaler backoff engaged after 2 failed attempts. Thresholds too aggressive for transient provisioning instability.
Customer traffic profile: bursty with many short-lived streams; batching config not optimal for this workload leading to higher kernel invocation overhead.
Observed 429s were from front-tier queueing, not explicit rate-limit policy; caused by lack of Ready capacity and request queue cap enforcement.
resolution: Mitigation applied 2026-03-10 03:40 UTC: replaced faulty AMI on node group and reprovisioned 3 nodes with correct GPU drivers; cordoned and drained two impacted nodes.
Mitigation applied 2026-03-10 04:15 UTC: moved noisy tenant-3142 to overflow capacity and limited their allowed concurrent streams (temporary quota) to reduce PCIe contention.
Customer-facing workaround: temporarily increased fallback to redwood-open-1.3b-quant for non-critical streams and enabled prefix caching to reduce token work.

Root cause: AMI rollback during recent infra maintenance introduced older GPU driver on new instances, combined with a noisy tenant co-located on the same dedicated pool causing degraded node throughput.

Permanent fixes planned: 1) pin AMI build in auto-provisioner and add driver check in node health probe; 2) implement PCIe contention alerting for node-level telemetry; 3) adjust autoscaler backoff to retry with shorter backoff for node-provisioner class failures; 4) implement tenant isolation policy for dedicated pools to prevent noisy co-tenancy in single node group.

Follow-ups created: INT-4021 (infra: AMI pin and driver probe), INT-4022 (telemetry: PCIe saturation alerting), SUP-7860 (customer: postmortem follow-up and quota adjustment request from StreamScribe).
